# Results — Study 883 (Mid-Cap Sweet Spot)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — mid-caps
are the "forgotten middle", a better **risk-adjusted** return than either large (SPY) or
small (IWM), so the mid-cap ETF (IJH / MDY) should deliver an **excess-of-cash Sharpe
advantage over BOTH**. Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py`
to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month; the
partial current month is dropped). Fingerprint `d294f0cdb517` (total-return close panel).*

*Data as-of 2026-06-30 · Fingerprint `d294f0cdb517`.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily closes (`auto_adjust=True`, **total-return**): IJH, MDY, SPY, IWM, BIL — 1993-01-29 → 2026-06-30, 8,411 dated rows |
| Mid-cap legs | **IJH** (iShares Core S&P Mid-Cap 400, 2000-05+) primary; **MDY** (SPDR S&P MidCap 400, 1995-05+) same index, longest tape |
| Neighbours | **SPY** (S&P 500, large) and **IWM** (Russell 2000, small) |
| Cash leg | **BIL** (SPDR 1-3 Month T-Bill, 2007-05+) — every Sharpe is **excess-of-cash** |

| Statistics | excess-vs-excess Sharpe race; Newey-West (HAC) *t* on the pairwise daily return difference (cash cancels → full IJH/MDY tape); a paired circular-block-bootstrap (2,000×, 21-day blocks) CI on the Sharpe advantage; a four-era cut; a costed dollar-neutral spread; a 20-seed synthetic control |

**Short history — named on the Signal axis.** BIL, the cash leg, only lists from 2007-05, so
the *excess-of-cash Sharpe race* is a **2007-2026** window (it misses the 1995-2006 era when
mid-caps most out-ran large). The pairwise return **difference** (mid − large) is
cash-independent, so the era-robustness cut reaches the full MDY tape back to **1995**.

## The race — excess-of-cash Sharpe (2007-2026 common window)

| leg | ann. return | ann. vol | **excess-of-cash Sharpe** | max drawdown |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **IJH** (mid) | +11.58% | 22.5% | **0.453** | −55.1% |
| MDY (mid, twin) | +11.46% | 22.9% | 0.440 | −55.3% |
| **SPY** (large) | +12.12% | 19.8% | **0.542** | −55.2% |
| **IWM** (small) | +11.15% | 24.8% | **0.394** | −58.6% |

Mid-cap sits **literally in the middle**: IJH's excess Sharpe (0.453) is *below* large SPY
(0.542) and only *just above* small IWM (0.394). Over the modern common window the
"sweet spot" claim fails on its own terms — the large-cap mega-tech era handed SPY the best
risk-adjusted return, not the middle. Mid does *not* beat BOTH.

## The advantage — mid (IJH) excess-Sharpe minus each neighbour, paired bootstrap

| pair | Sharpe advantage | 95% CI (2,000× block bootstrap) | verdict |
|---|--:|--:|:--:|
| IJH − SPY | **−0.089** | [−0.225, +0.050] | **spans 0** (mid *trails* large) |
| IJH − IWM | **+0.060** | [−0.038, +0.169] | **spans 0** |

Neither advantage clears zero. Mid's edge over small is positive but statistically
indistinguishable from none; its "edge" over large is *negative*.

## Pairwise return difference — cash-independent, so the full tape

The difference `mid − large` doesn't need the cash leg, so it reaches back to each pair's
start:

| pair | mean diff | HAC *t* | window |
|---|--:|--:|:--|
| IJH − SPY | +1.74%/yr | +1.19 | 2000-05 → 2026-06 (n=6,560) |
| IJH − IWM | +0.44%/yr | +0.38 | 2000-05 → 2026-06 |
| **MDY − SPY** | +0.95%/yr | +0.67 | **1995-05 → 2026-06 (n=7,839)** |
| MDY − IWM | +0.32%/yr | +0.27 | 2000-05 → 2026-06 |

Mid *does* out-return both neighbours on average over the very long run — the "forgotten
middle" tilt is real in **sign** — but **not one difference clears HAC *t* = 2**. Over 31
years of the longest mid-vs-large tape the +0.95%/yr gap carries a *t* of only +0.67.

## Robustness — MDY − SPY by era (the myth-check)

| era | mean diff | HAC *t* | n |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1995-01 → 2003-01 | +3.21%/yr | +0.94 | 1,929 |
| 2003-01 → 2010-01 | +3.94%/yr | +1.48 | 1,763 |
| 2010-01 → 2017-01 | +1.49%/yr | +0.74 | 1,762 |
| **2017-01 → 2026-07** | **−3.50%/yr** | **−1.23** | 2,385 |

The sweet-spot tilt lived in **1995-2016** (mid beat large by +1.5 to +3.9%/yr, though never
significantly) and then **inverted**: through the 2017-2026 mega-cap era large *beat* mid by
−3.5%/yr. The advantage is not a stable structural premium — it is an era-dependent tilt that
the last decade reversed.

## The costed spread — long mid / short neighbour (dollar-neutral)

Charge = 50 bps/yr borrow on the short leg + 2 sides × 3 bps one-way × 4 rebalances/yr
(IJH, SPY, IWM are all cheap, penny-spread mega-ETFs):

| trade | gross | charge | **net** | HAC *t* (net) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| long IJH / short SPY | +1.74%/yr | 0.74% | **+1.00%/yr** | +0.68 |
| long IJH / short IWM | +0.44%/yr | 0.74% | **−0.30%/yr** | −0.25 |

The only positive net (long-mid/short-large, +1.00%/yr) carries a net *t* of +0.68 — nowhere
near bankable — and it is exactly the leg that **reversed** in the last decade. Long-mid /
short-small nets *negative*. Nothing survives costs with any statistical claim.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic seeded daily world: a common market factor drives large/mid/small (betas
0.90/1.00/1.20); the knob `edge` lifts the **mid** leg's excess-of-cash mean. No network.

| world | mid adv vs large | mid adv vs small | beats both? |
|---|--:|--:|:--:|
| null (`edge = 0`), 20 seeds | mean −0.018 | — | strict-significant in **1/20** (~nominal 5%) |
| planted (`edge = 0.0006`, seed 883) | **+1.011** (*t* = +5.78) | **+1.110** (*t* = +5.02) | **yes** |

With a genuine planted edge the detector cleanly finds mid beating BOTH neighbours at HAC
*t* ≈ 5; on the null it essentially never fires. So the real-tape "no robust advantage"
result is a true reading of the tape, not a dead detector. *(Machinery / power check only —
never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** The "mid-caps are the risk-adjusted sweet spot, better than BOTH large
  and small" claim does **not** clear a robust bar. On the excess-of-cash Sharpe race
  (2007-2026) mid sits **in the middle** — IJH 0.453, *below* SPY's 0.542 and barely above
  IWM's 0.394 — so it fails the "over BOTH" test outright; both bootstrap Sharpe-advantage
  CIs span zero. The long-run return tilt is **sign-correct** (mid out-returned both, +0.95
  to +1.74%/yr) but **never significant** (best HAC *t* = +1.19 over 26 years) and it
  **reversed** in 2017-2026 (−3.5%/yr vs large). A real but fragile, era-dependent tilt —
  not a dependable premium. *(Short cash history: the Sharpe race misses the 1995-2006 mid
  heyday — named on the Signal axis.)*
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** No costed spread clears the bar. Long-mid/short-large nets
  +1.00%/yr but at net *t* = +0.68 (and on the leg that inverted post-2017);
  long-mid/short-small nets **−0.30%/yr**. The Sharpe "advantage" over small is a
  lower-return, similar-vol artifact, not a paid premium — a Mirage after costs.
